what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours that bought real epistemic machinery and moved the thesis not at all, and the two halves need saying separately. **What was bought is good and some of it is the best kind.** The constants gate the director asked for landed and mechanically found three of his four examples on its first run — one legal VAT rule declared seven times in two different SHAPES (a scalar 0.05 in `company/billing/invoice.py`, a per-segment table in `saas/non_commodity.py`), a standing charge of 53.0 p/day that is neither published fuel average but very nearly their sum, about £95/yr, and `MAX_CHURN_PROBABILITY` at 1.0 on one side of the seam and 0.95 on the other. It was filed BLOCKING and taken down to LATENT by measuring exposure rather than inferring it: zero invoice rows, no live caller, no feed reads `compare_tariffs`. The standing rule `INDEPENDENCE_IS_NOT_INFERENCE` was applied UNPROMPTED to a second figure and found that "where the company does worse than guessing" is three threshold crossings, two of them 3.4% and 3.9% past the line with n=20 behind one of them — a coin flip ordering the build queue. And C3 was pre-registered, measured in an isolated worktree, and **refuted in the direction I named**: I predicted the shown price would push the departure level DOWN and it went UP in five years, kept beside the prediction rather than revised. That is the discipline working. **What was not bought is everything the thesis is judged on, and one by-product is worse than the experiment that found it.** The departure-level anchor was fitted to each band's HIGH endpoint — the right anti-flattering choice — and the consequence went unnoticed: the world's realised rate sits on the exact top of its band **ten years out of ten, with zero headroom above**. So any upward move of any size fails the control, a +0.11pp change that moved zero departures "leaves the published band", and downward resolution runs 0.6pp to 3.6pp depending on how wide that year's published range happens to be — in the direction that favours us. The largest fidelity claim this project has made rests on a control that can only fail one way and cannot size anything. Meanwhile on the company's side of the wall NOTHING moved: `company/crm/market_conditions.py` still asserts 34.9% switching for 2016 against a published 17.0–17.6%, live, scaling every enriched churn estimate — and the co-calibration guard I rebuilt independently confirmed it, company outside the band 8 of 10 years by up to 17.3pp. **I named that in focus twice now and it has been drawn zero times**, so per my own rule the steer is the thing drifting and it moves up rather than being restated. Two of four focus items went undrawn, both lane 0. And none of it reaches a reader: publishing has been wedged **17.9 hours across 16 episodes**, and I now know exactly why BY NAME rather than by guess — a `level_current 0->2` on `PB3_book_growth_as_earned_outcome` sits staged in the shared maturity map with `simulation/run_phase2b.py` in its file_scope, uncommitted, so the level gate correctly refuses every publish commit and no draw priority can ever clear it because the publisher cannot carry another lane's source. The one-line read: **we got measurably better at knowing when we are wrong, and no better at showing we are right.**

One thing the document establishes that changes the question you asked: past 2025 the world does not become UNANCHORED, it becomes FROZEN. Every year from 2026 returns identical numbers forever — multiplier 1.114, departure rate 17.93%, anchor 3.021 — so a company predicting a constant meets a constant, its churn belief is trivially right, and the measured "skill" is an artefact of a world with no variance to predict. for_the_director.recommendation: Route A at high frequency, route B at low, and the boundary marked on every figure. Prices, demand, weather and grid intensity have 10³–10⁵ observations and can support a real shape test, which is also where the interesting futures live. The annual behavioural calibrations have TEN annual points and cannot support a claim about autocorrelation or regime persistence, so past 2025 they are declared constant and declared unvalidated — which is what they already are; the change is that it stops being silent. I am not waiting on you for the two pieces that are mine and I have started neither: making the 2025/2026 boundary a first-class fact on artefacts, and ensuring nothing quotes a post-2025 figure beside a measured one without the marker. Both make our figures look more provisional, not less.
